Subject: SI onboarding kick-off — data residency and escrow requirements

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the onboarding call yesterday. As we scoped internal work for Nexa's EU and APAC clients, a couple of items came up on the vendor side that we need to lock down before we start implementation:

- Data escrow: customers in Germany and Japan want a vendor-neutral escrow arrangement and an SLA describing retrieval timelines if Redwood ever terminates service. Can you share a draft SLA or precedent?
- Egress and routing: for APAC customers we need clarity on egress IP ranges and whether traffic can be forced through local cloud connectors (GCP Tokyo / Azure Japan East).
- KMS/Key custody: some customers insist keys remain in-custody for their region (Azure Key Vault / CloudHSM). Will Redwood support bring-your-own-key in private deployments?

I've attached a short checklist and what customers asked for (Data_Escrow_SLA_draft.pdf). Can you point me to the right contacts on your side so we can map responsibilities?

Appreciate it — happy to take a 30m sync if that helps.

Cheers,
Sarah
Head of Partnerships, Nexa Systems

- We have a standard vendor-escrow template and can provide a draft SLA; it needs minor edits per customer jurisdiction.

Camila / Sarah — technical clarifications below. I'm pasting the short answers first, then details for Nexa and their clients.

Short answers:
- Escrow SLA: security can produce a vendor-neutral escrow template within 3 business days. Legal will need to review for Germany/Japan-specific retention language (likely 2–3 additional business days).
- Egress IPs & routing: we'll provide a CIDR list and a per-region NAT table. For Private deployments you can configure per-customer NATs; for Dedicated we can reserve regional NAT pools.
- BYOK/KMS: BYOK supported in Private via KMIP-compatible HSMs and cloud KMS key wrapping. For Hosted we support customer-managed KMS integrations via shared responsibility model but HSM import is restricted.

Details / notes: 
1) Escrow mechanics: we keep an incremental copy of customer model artifacts and metadata (no customer PII) in an encrypted escrow store. We recommend customers pick a neutral escrow agent; we can sign standard hold instructions. The SLA draft will include retrieval windows (48h for manifests, 7 business days for full deposit with insured shipment).
2) Data flows & routing: for APAC customers that require traffic to stay within region we recommend Private deployment in-region. If customers use Dedicated, we can add a regional egress enforcement layer but must coordinate with cloud provider peering. Expect a 2–3 week lead time for reserved NATs and peering.
3) KMS specifics: list of supported key stores will be in KMS_Map.xlsx. For highly regulated customers we'd recommend colocating a CloudHSM in the same region with key policies that deny export.

I'll attach the draft network diagram and KMS map — Marcus helped compile.

-David
Director, Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
